capture_source: live 2026-11-08: NW RFC SDK client (pyrfc) with CommonCryptoLib over SNC against an S/4HANA lab system; the decrypted plaintext of the first wrapped message (the logon) in three modes. User DEVELOPER has an SNC name mapped to the client certificate.
evidence: tier 1. Only the record tags and which of them are empty are kept; no values (user name, password, host names) are recorded.
notes: snc_sso=0 with a password: 0x0111 (user) and 0x0117 (scrambled password) present, plus an empty 0x0675 between 0x0115 and 0x0501.
snc_sso=1: 0x0117 and 0x0675 absent; 0x0111 present only when a user is given. Both snc_sso=1 runs logged on (as the mapped user).
The SNC frames themselves were identical across the three modes: header lengths 0x96/0x18/0x18 and the same QOP fields. No extension header carries anything SSO-related.
With a user given and snc_sso=1, a wrong password still logged on: the password is not sent.
